question.question: Can a locally produced append-completion marker from an earlier raft term remove unstable entries when consumed after a real authority transition, even if its entry index/log term still matches?
question.importance: Removing unstable entries on an obsolete storage context can make later reads depend on stable storage while older writes are still in flight. The selected requirement is the documented local context fence; a consensus divergence or crash-loss consequence requires additional replacement and endpoint evidence.

question.trigger_rationale: The acquired producer documentation explicitly distinguishes raft term from retained entry term. Exploration produced two stale markers whose index/log term still matched, plus a fresh-term HardState-only marker for that same entry identity. This permits a discriminating local check without fabricating critical state.

obligation.description: For an authentic snapshot-free local append-completion response generated in an earlier raft term and returned after its ordered append work has completed, consuming that response in a later raft term must not truncate the unstable entry prefix, even when its entry index and log term match the current unstable log.

scope.description: AsyncStorageWrites RawNode entry-completion consumption across increasing raft terms, with serialized state-machine access and contract-compliant ordered local append work.
assumptions: Response was produced by the same RawNode instance and returned unchanged after its storage work completed.
No crash/restart of that instance between marker production and consumption.
Response has no snapshot and no event interleaves within its synchronous Step call.
excluded: Crash durability and stable-storage overwrite consequences

grounding.derivation: S_COMPLETION_EXPECTATION explicitly states that a response returned after its raft term changes is ignored and the unstable log is not truncated. S_STABLE_EXPECTATION restricts stableTo to callers that can attest no in-progress overwrite, explaining why entry identity alone is insufficient. This is a documented implementation responsibility, not an obligation inferred from observing the Step guard. The requirement narrows to the entry portion and excludes snapshots because S_DISPATCH deliberately processes old-term snapshot completion. Fresh-term stabilization is a permitted control, not an equality or eventual-success requirement.
grounding.applicability: S_CONFIG requires ordered local writes and response release after completion in async mode. RawNode.Step accepts locally sourced storage responses. A delayed authentic marker remains a legal input after a term change; the selected safety requirement applies independently of whether an overwrite actually occurs.
alternatives: The separate index/log-term match is an additional protection but cannot replace the documented raft-term fence.
Fresh-term HardState-only markers can stabilize the same entry identity; excluding all old-entry-term markers would incorrectly strengthen the requirement.

feedback.answered: Exploration completed with real elections from leader 1 term 2 to leader 2 term 3. Node 3 held two term-2 markers for entry (index 3, log term 2); delivering them at term 3 kept unstable offset 3. A term-3 marker from an append carrying zero entries advanced offset to 4; later term-3 completion advanced to 5. Final observed applied and committed indexes were 4. These are exploratory observations, not a formal property result.
